deep.reconstruction: This page has no mathematics. It is a draft faculty vote (Votum) in German, written in pencil with many deletions. It is headed 'Riemann 26', apparently a running number in a faculty circulation file, and has '128' in the margin (the folio number). The context is a motion (Antrag) in the Göttingen Philosophical Faculty about prize questions under a foundation ('im Sinne des Stifters'). The statutes of that foundation exclude 'speculative philosophy'. This fits the Beneke prize foundation, set up in memory of the anti-speculative philosopher and psychologist Friedrich Eduard Beneke; that identification is my inference. Riemann's points are these. (1) He also thinks accepting the motion serves the interest of science. A deleted phrase refers to a position of his colleague Lotze. (2) The clause excluding speculative philosophy does not require restricting the questions mainly to philosophical theory. In the founder's spirit (the founder apparently refers to his brother), the aim should rather be to promote psychology, ethics, a branch of applied philosophy (Rechts- or Religionsphilosophie; the reading is uncertain) and pedagogy. (3) If representatives of the other subjects, and not only the professor of philosophy, are to set and judge philosophical prize questions, the rotation (Turnus) should be extended to all members of the faculty. Representatives of some subjects (abbreviated, illegible) would be free to decline. The previous page in the bundle is an unrelated draft report on Baeyer's Mitteleuropäische Gradmessung, so the bundle mixes administrative drafts. There is no derivation to reconstruct.

results.what: Administrative opinion on the scope of philosophical prize questions and on extending the setting/judging rotation to all faculty members

deep.surprise_reason: Non-mathematical faculty administrative draft. Riemann's participation in Göttingen faculty business (votes on foundations and prizes) is documented and unremarkable. The only point of mild interest is biographical: his view that empirical philosophy (psychology, ethics, pedagogy) fits the founder's intent, and his reference to Lotze.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 probably reads '...im Interesse der Wissenschaft zu befürworten', with a struck continuation on line 2 that mentions 'des Herrn Collegen Lotze'.
The struck words before 'Theorie' look like 'philosophische' variants, with 'die' inserted above. The intended reading may be 'auf die philosophische Theorie'.
Line 4 ('der ... auf seinen ... beizugeben') more plausibly reads 'der ausdrücklich auf seinen Bruder Bezug nimmt, vielmehr die Förderung der Psycho-' (tentative).
'Rechtsphilosophie' is uncertain and could be 'Religionsphilosophie'. F. E. Beneke wrote on both natural law and pedagogy, so context does not decide it.
The superscript '128' at the right margin is the folio number, not part of the text.
In the last line, 'den den Vertretern' is a duplication. The abbreviated subject designation (an initial letter, possibly a single capital) is illegible.
